title: check:all executa a suite inteira 3x (test, coverage, skip-ratchet): colapsar numa execucao unica
description:
MEDIDO em 2026-08-03. scripts/check-all.ts tem 14 gates e TRES executam a suite completa (~5936 testes, ~134s cada): o gate 'test' roda bun test; o gate 'coverage' faz Bun.spawnSync(bun test --coverage) em check-coverage.ts:131; o gate 'skip-ratchet' faz Bun.spawnSync(bun test) em check-skip-ratchet.ts:268. Um check:all = 3 execucoes completas, ~400s onde 134s bastaria. O CI paga uma QUARTA (.github/workflows/ci.yml:81, test-in-container.ts). Evidencia empirica no gate-results.json antigo: gate 'test' 34511ms vs gate 'coverage' 34381ms, duracoes quase identicas, ou seja coverage paga corrida nova em vez de reusar.

IMPOSTO RECORRENTE POR CICLO (criterio de admissao de alvo interno): o worker roda check:all por story e a mediana de worker rounds por ciclo subiu de 2 para 7 desde 24/07; o reviewer tambem roda. No review do CAM-482 foram 4 execucoes completas, ~6,7 min dos 30 de teto, 22 por cento do orcamento de review em redundancia pura, contribuindo direto para o teto ser batido 5 vezes seguidas sem veredito.

A REDUNDANCIA E ESTRUTURAL, NAO INERENTE: coverage precisa da saida de bun test --coverage e skip-ratchet precisa da linha de sumario de skip/pass; ambas ja sao produzidas por UMA invocacao de bun test --coverage. Os dois scripts consumidores JA aceitam funcoes de saida injetaveis (check-skip-ratchet.ts:83), entao a costura existe.

ESCOPO: colapsar as tres execucoes em uma. NAO deletar teste: a suite foi medida em 2,08x test:src LOC (topo do normal), PLANA desde 15/07, com 0 testes pulados. O problema e execucao, nao volume. Cada um dos tres gates precisa continuar falhando pela sua propria condicao, com os oraculos varridos VERMELHOS contra a main (regra CAM-372).

spec.scope: Collapse the three full test-suite executions that happen inside ONE `bun run check:all` into a single `bun test --coverage` run, owned by check-all.ts, whose captured output feeds the coverage and skip-ratchet gates in-process. Today check-all spawns `bun test` (gate test), then `bun scripts/check-coverage.ts` which internally spawns `bun test --coverage` (check-coverage.ts:131), then `bun scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts` which internally spawns `bun test` (check-skip-ratchet.ts:268). DECIDED MECHANISM (in-process, no fallback): check-all stops spawning the two consumer scripts as subprocesses and instead calls their exported entries with the captured output injected -- checkCoverage({ getCoverage: () => parseCoverageOutput(captured) }) and checkSkipRatchet({ getSuiteOutput: () => captured }). Both DI seams already exist (GetSuiteOutputFn is raw-string typed at check-skip-ratchet.ts:84; parseCoverageOutput is exported and pure at check-coverage.ts:87), and test-in-container.ts:238-240 is the existing production precedent for feeding pre-captured output to the skip checks without a second run. The in-process form is chosen over an env-var/tmpfile IPC form on merit: it eliminates the silent-degradation and stale-artifact failure classes BY CONSTRUCTION, because there is no fallback path to degrade into. Cost is higher (the flat Gate manifest stops being uniform, check-all.ts is at its file-size ceiling of 176 and needs a raise with tracker ref, and the per-gate cmd/args assertions in test/check-all.test.ts must be restated); that cost is noted, not a reason to choose the weaker form. OUT OF SCOPE: the fourth suite run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:81, test-in-container.ts, container lane); deleting, skipping or reducing any test; changing coverage floors, skip expectations, or what any gate asserts.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 (change-detection, swept RED on main). One check:all issues exactly ONE suite spawn and ZERO consumer-script spawns. ORACLE, bracket-free by the CAM-474 rule so extraction cannot truncate it: bun -e "import { runGates } from './scripts/check-all.ts'; const log = new Array<string>(); runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => { log.push(c + ' ' + a.join(' ')); return { success: true, exitCode: 0 }; }) as never }); const suite = log.filter((l) => /^bun test( |$)/.test(l)).length; const cons = log.filter((l) => /check-(coverage|skip-ratchet)\.ts/.test(l)).length; console.log(suite === 1 && cons === 0 ? 'GREEN' : 'RED suite=' + suite + ' consumers=' + cons);" -- SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: prints 'RED suite=1 consumers=2', exit 0 (a real red, not a syntax/extraction failure). Must print GREEN after the change.

AC2 (change-detection). The single collapsed invocation is `bun test --coverage`, not plain `bun test`: it is the only argv whose output satisfies BOTH consumers. ORACLE: same spawn-log harness as AC1, asserting the one suite entry matches /^bun test --coverage( |$)/. Against main the suite entry is plain 'bun test' (check-all.ts:78), so this sweeps RED.

AC3 (change-detection, gate keeps its OWN failure condition). Given a shared suite output whose 'All files' row is below the floor in scripts/coverage-budget.json, the coverage gate reports fail, and NO additional suite spawn occurs while producing that verdict. Failing only because a second run was skipped, or passing because the output was empty, both violate this criterion.

AC4 (change-detection, gate keeps its OWN failure condition). Given a shared suite output whose skip count differs from the lane expectation in test/helpers/lane-expectations.json, the skip-ratchet gate reports fail, and NO additional suite spawn occurs while producing that verdict. All three of its existing failure modes must survive: skip delta (either sign), suite-did-not-report-a-tally, and pass-below-floor / too-tight-headroom.

AC5 (change-detection, anti-contamination). The test gate still fails for test failures ONLY. A failing test makes gate 'test' fail; a coverage floor breach makes gate 'coverage' fail while gate 'test' stays ok. MEASURED PREMISE 2026-08-03: there is no bunfig.toml and no coverageThreshold anywhere, and `bun test --coverage` on a deliberately failing test exits 1 exactly as plain `bun test` does, so the collapsed run's exit code carries test-failure signal only. If a coverage threshold is ever added to bunfig, this criterion breaks and the gates re-couple.

AC6 (anti-inert, fail-closed). If the shared suite output is empty, truncated, or missing the completion tally, BOTH the coverage and the skip-ratchet gates FAIL. Neither may pass, and neither may silently re-spawn the suite to recover. This exists because a collapse can ship INERT (the CAM-479 disease: fix shipped inert while grep-oracles read satisfied). ORACLE, verified against main 2026-08-03 as the property to preserve: bun -e "import { checkSkipRatchet } from './scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts'; import { checkCoverage, parseCoverageOutput } from './scripts/check-coverage.ts'; const out = ''; const sr = checkSkipRatchet({ getSuiteOutput: () => out }); const cv = checkCoverage({ getCoverage: () => parseCoverageOutput(out), getStagedDiff: () => '' }); console.log(sr.ok === false && cv.ok === false ? 'GREEN' : 'RED');" -- prints GREEN on main for both empty and garbage input. NOTE the asymmetry this pins: parseSkipCount returns 0 when the skip line is absent, which would fail OPEN on its own; only checkSuiteRan's positive-evidence tally guard (check-skip-ratchet.ts:224-234) makes it fail closed. That guard must not be removed or bypassed by the new wiring.

AC7 (invariance pin, green by construction, comparand derived from main at check time). Gate identity survives the collapse: gate-results.json still carries all three names 'test', 'coverage' and 'skip-ratchet' as independent rows with independent status fields, the GateResult key set stays exactly durationMs/name/status, and `bun run check:ci-parity` passes. The collapse is about EXECUTION, not about REPORTING: CI's step-summary table (.github/workflows/ci.yml:27-33) and check-ci-parity.ts (which imports GATES and enforces name parity) both key on these names.

AC8 (invariance pin). Standalone use is preserved and still self-sufficient: `bun scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts` and `bun scripts/check-coverage.ts`, run alone with no check-all around them, each still perform their own suite execution and reach the same verdict as before. The collapse must not make either script depend on being called from check-all.

AC9 (value criterion, measured not asserted). Wall-clock of one `bun run check:all` drops by at least one full suite execution versus main. Report the measured before/after totals and the per-gate durations from gate-results.json; after the change the 'coverage' and 'skip-ratchet' rows must be dramatically below the 'test' row, whereas on main gate 'test' and gate 'coverage' are near-identical (34511ms vs 34381ms in the recorded gate-results.json, which is the empirical fingerprint of the redundant run). Do not report a speedup without the two measurements.
gotchas: MEASURED 2026-08-03, load-bearing: `bun test --coverage` emits BOTH the coverage table AND the ` N pass` / ` N fail` / `Ran N tests across N file.` summary, and ALL of it goes to STDERR (stdout is empty). Capture and concatenate both streams, as both existing adapters already do (check-coverage.ts:132, check-skip-ratchet.ts:269). Capturing stdout alone yields an empty blob and both gates fail closed.

MEASURED 2026-08-03: the tally line is singular for a single file ('Ran 25 tests across 1 file.'). RAN_LINE_RE (check-skip-ratchet.ts:132) already tolerates this via `tests? across \d+ files?`. Do not tighten it.

The two parsers are mutually non-conflicting over one superset blob: coverage line-scans for /^All files\s*\|/ and ignores everything else; skip-ratchet uses /m-anchored regexes with a single-leading-space anchor (/^ (\d+) skip/m, /^ (\d+) pass/m) that a coverage table row can never match. So one combined output feeds both correctly. No fixture in the repo currently contains both shapes; the change should add one.

check-all.ts today spawns every gate with stdio fully INHERITED (check-all.ts:131), and the SpawnFn type bakes the 'inherit','inherit' generics in (check-all.ts:34). Capturing the suite output is therefore a TYPE-level change that also touches the test fakes in test/check-all.test.ts:33-43. Keep the operator's live progress visible (tee) rather than swallowing the suite output into silence.

scripts/check-all.ts is at its file-size ceiling of exactly 176 in scripts/file-size-budget.json. Raising it requires a tracker ref (CAM-488) in the STAGED diff or the file-size gate fails. scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts has no budget entry at all.

check-ci-parity.ts imports GATES from check-all.ts and enforces that every gate name is covered and every `bun run <X>` in ci.yml is allowlisted or a gate name. Renaming or removing a gate trips this gate. Keep the three names.

test/check-all.test.ts asserts cmd/args per gate (one assertion per gate) and test/gates-manifest.test.ts pins GATES length 14 and the name set. Gates that stop being plain spawns need those assertions RESTATED in terms of the new shape. Do NOT delete them to make the suite green.

DO NOT delete, skip, or thin any test. Measured: test:src ratio 2.08x (top of normal), flat since 2026-07-15, 0 skipped tests. The defect is redundant EXECUTION, not test volume. A PR that shrinks the suite has solved the wrong problem.

check-skip-ratchet has an env-driven lane selector (CAM_TEST_LANE, check-skip-ratchet.ts:94,170-172) defaulting to 'host'. The 'container' lane is measured by the separate scripts/test-in-container.ts path (the fourth CI run) which already feeds pre-captured output to checkSuiteRan/checkSkipCount without a second run. Leave the container lane alone.

Every oracle in these criteria is written bracket-free on purpose. A literal closing square bracket inside oracle probe text closes the oracle mark early because extractLastOracleRaw walks bracket depth (CAM-474). Build brackets via String.fromCharCode if one is unavoidable, and treat exit 2 or 'syntax error' as an EXTRACTION failure, never as a red criterion.

Fixing an over-fire is verified in BOTH directions (CAM-474): after any change that narrows or widens a gate's failure condition, re-measure both the true positives and the false positives in the same round. Narrowing a condition kills detection trivially.
